title: Shots, the John Casman band and Wooden Joe
summary: Vincent recalls cornetist Shots Madison, a pick-up band called the John Casman band, and Wooden Joe Nickerson's powerful blowing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Why not? Ask me if you knew shots.

Did you know shots? Shots, huh, Ruby? I was playing with him. Shots played with us in the full place. I was playing with him. Shots was another liquor-head, too. He was a good corner player, but he was a liquor-head. Shots drank so much whiskey to the kids. He played with us until he got kind of sick. And he wasn't sick so long before he died. He was a good corner player, Shots. Which band was that? Whose band? Well, we was a make-up band, I thought. We didn't have no special name. Then I was with, uh, called it the John Casman band at that time. And we had Wooden Joe. You ever heard of him talking? Wooden Joe and Albert Nickerson, that's his cousin. And Joe was named Nickerson, too, but we used to call him Wooden Joe. He wasn't much, you know, Wooden Joe. He said anything, only one kid. He was so strong. Woo! He could, but I think they called him Wooden Joe. He could blow so alive and blow so long, you know.
